📰 General

Google Expands Find Hub: Website Now Supports Tags and Headphones •

Google has launched a new website, findhub.google.com, to complement the existing Find Hub functionality within the Messages app. The website provides a centralized location for users to manage and locate Google Find tags and headphones. Previously, Find Hub primarily focused on locating lost devices through the Messages app. This expansion offers a more comprehensive solution for tracking Google’s Find accessories. The website mirrors the functionality of the android.com/find page.

🌍 World

EU Diplomats Bolster Ukraine’s War Crimes Tribunal with Strong Support •

EU diplomats convened in Kyiv to demonstrate unwavering support for the International Criminal Court’s investigation into alleged Russian war crimes in Ukraine. Twelve bloc foreign ministers and senior officials participated in the meetings, signaling a united front against alleged atrocities. All EU nations except Hungary committed to backing the tribunal, aiming to hold individuals accountable for war crimes. The gathering underscored the bloc’s commitment to justice and accountability in the ongoing conflict.

🦅 US

Trump Administration Rolls Back Endangered Species Protections for Gulf Drilling •

The Department of the Interior’s Office of Management and Budget issued a rule exempting oil and gas drilling in the Gulf of Mexico from regulations under the Endangered Species Act. This decision was prompted by concerns from the defense department that environmental lawsuits were impeding domestic energy production. The rule argues that the ESA’s protections could significantly disrupt offshore drilling operations. Critics argue this move undermines conservation efforts and prioritizes industry interests over environmental safeguards. The change is effective immediately, pending legal challenges.

💰 Business

OkCupid Shared 3 Million Photos with Facial Recognition Firm – Settlement Reached •

OkCupid, owned by Match Group, has reached a settlement with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) regarding the sharing of user photos with a facial recognition firm. The company admitted to failing to disclose that nearly 3 million user photos were provided to the company, which was developing a facial recognition system. As part of the settlement, OkCupid will not pay a fine, but must implement new privacy disclosures. The FTC investigation stemmed from concerns about user data privacy and the potential misuse of facial recognition technology.

💻 Technology

MindsEye CEO Reveals Disastrous Launch, Now Embracing a New Direction •

MindsEye CEO Mark Gerhard has stated that the game’s initial launch was the “worst launch ever,” citing overwhelmingly negative reviews and sales figures from 2025. The developer, Build a Rocket Boy, is now focusing on a new narrative direction for the open-world game. This shift involves developing a Cyberpunk 2077-style storyline, diverging from the original, poorly received release. Gerhard acknowledges the initial failure but expresses optimism about the game’s future trajectory.

🎭 Entertainment

Amazon Unveils First Trailer for “Masters of the Universe” Live-Action Film •

Amazon has released the first trailer for its upcoming live-action adaptation of “Masters of the Universe.” The trailer showcases the film’s visual style and introduces key characters, including Prince Adam/He-Man. The project is a collaboration between Amazon MGM and Mattel Studios, marking Mattel’s entry into live-action cinematic franchises. The film is set to premiere on July 20, 2024, and stars Kelsey Grammer as Skeletor.

🏅 Sports

Bulls’ Jaden Ivey Trade Woes Intensify, Karnišovas Faces Scrutiny •

The Chicago Bulls’ 2023-2024 season has been marked by significant struggles, including a sub-.400 record and numerous player injuries. The recent decision to waive point guard Jaden Ivey, acquired in a previous trade, further highlights the team’s difficulties. This move comes after a disappointing performance from Ivey and raises questions about Artūras Karnišovas’ management. The Bulls’ front office is facing increased scrutiny due to the series of unsuccessful moves this season.

🔬 Science

Orion Launch Reveals Renewed Optimism Amidst NASA’s Ambitious Space Station Plans •

Veteran observers at Kennedy Space Center reported a distinct shift in their perspective following the third successful launch of NASA’s Orion spacecraft. The launch, which tested the vehicle’s heat shield, was viewed with a newfound sense of optimism regarding NASA’s long-term goals. Specifically, the event fueled hope for the agency’s plans to construct a permanent space station in lunar orbit. The veteran observers noted the increased precision and overall performance of the launch as key factors contributing to this positive change.

🩺 Health

New COVID Variant, “Cicada,” Reemerges in U.S. After Initial South African Surge •

The COVID-19 variant nicknamed “Cicada” (BA.3.2) initially appeared in South Africa during late 2024, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). This variant was previously overcome by other strains but subsequently re-emerged and began causing infections within the United States. Scientists are currently monitoring its spread and assessing its characteristics, including its transmissibility and potential impact on vaccine effectiveness. Initial data suggests it exhibits increased transmissibility compared to previous Omicron subvariants.
